summary: Abdurrahman and Venkatesh prove that the central value of a symplectic L-function over a curve over a finite field is, up to squares, a global cohomological invariant. For X/F_q and ρ : π_1(X) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ) geometrically surjective, ℓ a finite field with #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8) and q ≡ 1 (mod 8) a square in the prime field of ℓ and prime to #Sp_{2r}(ℓ), L(X, ρ, q^{−1/2}) ≡ trace_X(ρ^*c_et) in ℓ^×/2, where c_et ∈ H^3(Sp_{2r}(ℓ), ℓ^×/2) is Soulé's étale Chern class (Theorem 3.1). The key input is a topological theorem (Theorem 2.1): for a closed oriented 3-manifold with a symplectic local system over any field of characteristic ≠ 2, the Reidemeister torsion square class equals ±∫ρ^*c_et. It is proved by bordism invariance, K-theory of number fields (Merkurjev–Suslin, Hutchinson–Tao), Chebotarev and an explicit example over Q(i). The arithmetic theorem is deduced from the topological one on Hurwitz stacks of Sp_{2r}(ℓ)-covers: their difference is a Dirichlet character (Step A), shown unramified outside 2ℓ by slicing Hilbert–Siegel modular varieties (Step B). The atlas plans the étale Chern class, Merkurjev–Suslin, spinor norms, Witt groups, PEL moduli and their compactifications, Weil II and tame specialization. It has nothing on Reidemeister torsion, Poincaré complexes, determinant functors with signs, oriented bordism, L-functions and ε-factors with torsion coefficients, Hurwitz stacks of unramified covers of curves, or the paper's moment-method slicing. Two new plans are proposed: the topological half (route A, new) and the arithmetic half (route B, a Part II of FunctionFieldArithmetic). Source routes send the finite-field Sp/SL homology lemmas to KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.1, Suslin's Hurewicz theorem and Hutchinson–Tao to K3BlochGroups, Chebotarev for arithmetic schemes to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4, and L-functions with finite coefficients to FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5. Two gaps in arXiv v1 reach the main theorem: Lemma 5.1.1 (and with it the proof of Theorem 3.1) fails for r = 1, #ℓ = 9, since H_2(SL_2(F_9), Z) = Z/3; and Lemma 5.2.1 applies (1.5) with finite coefficients, where the paper proves it only in characteristic 0. The base-change statement of Appendix B.10 holds only for the normalized torsion.

items.name: Group homology and cohomology, quadratic reciprocity, discriminants and Sylow subgroups
items.statement: Homology H_n(Γ, M) and cohomology H^n(Γ, M) of a discrete group Γ with coefficients in a Γ-module (here Z, Z/2 and trivial modules); the Legendre symbol and quadratic reciprocity, used in (4.1) and §5.5; the discriminant of a quadratic form with respect to a basis, whose square class is basis-independent; Sylow subgroups, used in §2.15.
items.note: Mathlib has group (co)homology of representations, quadratic reciprocity, QuadraticForm.discr and Sylow subgroups. It has no homology of classifying spaces B Sp(R) as spaces, no oriented bordism and no stable groups Sp(R) = lim Sp_{2r}(R).

items.name: The spinor norm
items.statement: For a nondegenerate quadratic space (W, q) over a field K of characteristic ≠ 2, the spinor norm O(W) → K^×/2 is the unique homomorphism sending the reflection in a nondegenerate vector v to the square class of ⟨v, v⟩; it is used on SO(W).
items.note: SpinRepresentations Layer 2 plans the spinor-norm exact sequence SO(Q) → K^×/(K^×)² over a general field. Zassenhaus's formula (item on Appendix B.9) is not planned there.

items.name: Quadratic spaces, discriminant and Witt group
items.statement: The discriminant disc(W) ∈ K^×/2 of a nondegenerate quadratic space, the square class of det⟨x_i, x_j⟩; split (hyperbolic) spaces and Lagrangians, with disc of a 2g-dimensional space with a Lagrangian equal to (−1)^g; the Witt group W_K.
items.note: QuadraticFormInvariants Layers 1 and 4 plan hyperbolic planes, Witt cancellation and the Witt ring; Mathlib has QuadraticForm.discr.

items.name: The étale Chern class c_et (Soulé's c_31)
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring with 2 invertible and Γ = Sp_{2r}(R), acting trivially on Spec R and on the trivial bundle R^{2r}. The equivariant étale Chern class c_2 ∈ H^4_Γ(Spec R, μ_2) gives by cap product Soulé's homomorphism c_et = c_31 : H_3(Sp_{2r}(R), μ_2) → H^1(R, μ_2) = H^1_et(Spec R, μ_2); when either side is finite, dually a class c_et ∈ H^3(Sp_{2r}(R), H^1(R, μ_2)). It is natural in R (for f : R → S the two composites H_3(BSp(R), Z/2) → H^1(S, μ_2) agree) and compatible with Sp_{2r} ⊂ Sp_{2r+2}, so it is defined on Sp(R). For a finite field ℓ it is a class in H^3(Sp_{2r}(ℓ), ℓ^×/2).
items.note: MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8 plans étale Chern classes of K-theory. The group-homology form on H_3(BSp(R)), its naturality diagram (§2.5) and the Bockstein compatibility used in (1.10) are to be derived from it.

items.name: Merkurjev–Suslin: surjectivity of the étale Chern class on indecomposable K_3
items.statement: For a field F of characteristic ≠ 2, the étale Chern class K_3(F)^ind → H^1(F, Z_2(2))/2^n is surjective for every n ≥ 1 (Merkurjev–Suslin Prop. 11.5; Weibel Thm. 5.5).
items.note: MotivicEtaleKTheory M.7 plans the identification of K_{2j−1} with H^1 of twist j, with corrected statements at 2. The statement at the prime 2 used here must be part of it.

items.name: Hilbert–Siegel moduli schemes 𝒮 with real multiplication and their compactifications
items.statement: For a totally real field F with [F:Q] ≥ 3, an integer e prime to m and ℓ, and Δ = D_F·e·ℓ: the smooth scheme 𝒮 over Z[1/Δ] representing r-dimensional abelian schemes with o_F-action, a positivity-preserving isomorphism of the trivial narrow ideal class with Hom_{o_F}(A, A*), and full level-e structure (e large). Its Q-fibre S has geometric components defined over Q(ζ_e); S(C) is a finite union of quotients of 𝔥_r^{[F:Q]} by level-e subgroups of the symplectic group of a projective o_F-module of rank 2r. S admits the Baily–Borel compactification, whose boundary has codimension ≥ 3 since [F:Q] ≥ 3, and 𝒮 admits Lan's relative toroidal compactification over Z[1/Δ] with normal crossings boundary.
items.note: PELModuli M1–M2 plan the moduli functors and their representability and smoothness; ShimuraVarieties V2 plans the Baily–Borel compactification with its boundary stratification, from which the codimension count r·[F:Q] follows; ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans the integral toroidal (Lan) compactifications.

items.name: Specialization of the tame fundamental group of a curve
items.statement: For a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, lifted to a smooth projective curve X_W over the Witt vectors W, the inclusion of the special fibre induces an isomorphism on the prime-to-p fundamental groups (SGA 1 X Thm. 2.1); in particular the prime-to-p quotient of the geometric fundamental group of a genus-g curve is the prime-to-p completion of a genus-g surface group.
items.note: InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.1 plans tame quotients and specialization maps for smooth proper families.

items.name: Weil II: weights, purity and semisimplicity
items.statement: For a pure lisse sheaf on a smooth variety over a finite field, its geometric monodromy is semisimple (Weil II Thm. 3.4.1(iii)), so the Zariski closure has reductive identity component; compactly supported cohomology of a sheaf of weights ≤ w has weights ≤ w + i in degree i; hence for the weight −1 systems here L(X, ρ, t) has no zeros in |t| < 1.
items.note: DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.7 plans the direct-image weight theorem and DWP.8 the geometric semisimplicity.

items.name: The Reidemeister torsion square class RT(M, ρ)
items.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, M a closed oriented (2k+1)-manifold and ρ a local system of K-vector spaces with a locally constant symplectic pairing (k odd), or a nondegenerate orthogonal pairing with a self-dual volume form and even rank (k even). The cochain complex C of M with coefficients in ρ has a (−1)^k-symmetric Poincaré pairing C ⊗ C → K[−2k−1] and a distinguished element of the determinant line [C] (from any triangulation; independent of the triangulation). Composing with the canonical [C] ≅ [H^*C] and the identification [H^*C] ≅ [τ_{>k}H]^{⊗2} from Poincaré duality gives RT(M, ρ) ∈ K^×/2. If ρ is acyclic it is, up to sign, the classical Reidemeister torsion modulo squares.
items.note: The sign conventions are fixed in Appendix B.

items.name: The Reidemeister torsion class over a normal ring
items.statement: For R a normal integral domain with 1/2 ∈ R and ρ with finitely generated projective fibres (of even rank, with self-dual volume form, in the orthogonal case) carrying a (−1)^k-symmetric pairing, RT(M, ρ ⊗ K) lies in the image of the injection H^1(R, μ_2) → H^1(K, μ_2), defining RT(M, ρ) ∈ H^1(R, μ_2). The normalized class (−1)^{χ_{1/2}(M,ρ)/2}RT(M, ρ) (dim M = 3) is compatible with base change R → S to normal integral rings.
items.note: Stated as corrected: the paper asserts base-change compatibility for RT itself, which fails when the semicharacteristic jumps (sourceIssues E19). The class comes from 𝔞 = ⊗(det C_i)^{(−1)^i} of a strictified complex (Appendix A.6.2).

items.name: Semicharacteristic and orientation reversal
items.statement: With χ_{1/2}(M, ρ) := Σ_{j≤k} (−1)^j dim H^j(M, ρ), RT(M^op, ρ) = (−1)^{χ_{1/2}(M, ρ)} RT(M, ρ), where M^op is M with the opposite orientation.

items.name: Evenness of the semicharacteristic in dimension 3
items.statement: For a closed oriented 3-manifold M and a symplectic local system ρ over a field (or, mod 2, over any ring with 2 invertible), χ_{1/2}(M, ρ) = dim H^0(M, ρ) − dim H^1(M, ρ) is even.
items.note: Proof sketched: χ_{1/2} mod 2 is a bordism invariant, giving H_3(Sp_{2r}(R), Z) → Z/2 natural in R; it vanishes on finite fields since F_q → F_{q²} induces zero on H_3(Sp(F_q), Z/2). Sawin–Wood give another proof.

items.name: Reidemeister torsion on the circle
items.statement: For M = S^1 and ρ with monodromy A ∈ SO(V), V an even-dimensional quadratic space over K with square discriminant, the fixed space of A has even dimension h and, when char K = 0, RT(S^1, ρ) = (−1)^{h/2}·spinor norm(A).
items.note: The paper proves this in characteristic 0 and says it likely holds in general.

items.name: Bordism invariance of Reidemeister torsion (Theorem 2.2)
items.statement: If N is a compact oriented manifold of dimension 4j (j ≥ 1) with oriented boundary M = ∂N and ρ is a symplectic local system on N, then (−1)^{χ_{1/2}(M, ρ)/2} RT(M, ρ|_M) = 1 in K^×/2. The case used is dim N = 4.
items.note: The printed statement says '4r-manifold' (sourceIssues E2); Appendix B.8 proves it for N of dimension 2k, k even. The sign presupposes that χ_{1/2}(M, ρ) is even, which §2.3.4 proves for dim M = 3.

items.name: Oriented bordism equals homology in degrees ≤ 3
items.statement: For a CW complex X and d ≤ 3, the map MSO_d(X) → H_d(X, Z), (M, f) ↦ f_*[M], is an isomorphism (Thom).
items.note: Cited as [Thom, 8, Thm. IV.13].

items.name: The Reidemeister-torsion transformation 𝔑 : 𝓑 → 𝓗
items.statement: On normal integral Z[1/2]-algebras R put 𝓑(R) = H_3(BSp(R), Z)/2 and 𝓗(R) = H^1(R, μ_2). The normalized torsion (M, ρ) ↦ (−1)^{χ_{1/2}(M,ρ)/2} RT(M, ρ) is an oriented-bordism invariant of 3-manifolds with symplectic R-local systems; with MSO_3 = H_3 it defines a homomorphism 𝔑 : 𝓑(R) → 𝓗(R), natural in R (diagram (2.8)), with 𝔑(ρ_*[M]) the normalized torsion of (M, ρ).

items.name: Lemma 2.7.1: degree-three homology of Sp_{2r}(F_q) and SL_{2r}(F_q) mod 2
items.statement: For q an odd prime power, the inclusion Sp_{2r} → SL_{2r} induces an isomorphism H_3(Sp_{2r}(F_q), Z)/2 → H_3(SL_{2r}(F_q), Z)/2 of groups of order 2; H_2(Sp_{2r}(F_q), Z) and H_2(SL_{2r}(F_q), Z) have odd order, so H_3(−, Z)/2 = H_3(−, Z/2).
items.note: Proof by Quillen's spectral sequence for the Lang fibration G → B(G(F_q)) → BG and H^3(Sp_{2r}, Z/2) ≅ H^3(SL_{2r}, Z/2). Stated as corrected: the paper claims H_2 = 0, which fails for SL_2(F_9) (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Lemma 2.7.2: c_et is an isomorphism for finite fields
items.statement: For every finite field F_q of odd characteristic, c_et : H_3(Sp_{2r}(F_q), Z)/2 → F_q^×/2 is an isomorphism of groups of order 2.
items.note: Uses Weibel [Thm. 5.1]: c_et : K_3(F_q)/2 → F_q^×/2 is an isomorphism; c_et factors through H_3(SL(F_q)) since BSL(F_q)^+ → BGL(F_q)^+ is a π_3-isomorphism.

items.name: Good finite fields
items.statement: For a finite field k of odd characteristic, 𝓑(k) and 𝓗(k) have order 2 and c_et is an isomorphism, so on k either 𝔑 = c_et or 𝔑 = 0. Put ε_k = 1 (k is good) in the first case and ε_k = 0 otherwise; a single symplectic local system over k with nonsquare Reidemeister torsion shows k is good.

items.name: Chebotarev density for arithmetic schemes
items.statement: For a normal integral ring S finitely generated over Z with a geometric base point, the Frobenius elements of the closed points are dense in π_1(Spec S) (Serre, Lectures on N_X(p), §9; Pink, App. B); the closed points x of S, weighted by log q_x, have natural density (in the normalization of §2.14) and a Z/2-cover split at a density-one set of closed points is trivial.
items.note: Serre's density theorem for schemes of finite type over Z; PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 routes the same theorem to AN.4.

items.name: Lemma 2.9.1: the transfer lemma
items.statement: Let k_0, k_1 be finite fields and α_i ∈ H^1(k_i, μ_2) nonzero. If a normal integral finitely generated ring S with maps φ_i : S → k_i carries a c_et-liftable class α_S ∈ H^1(S, μ_2) (α_S = c_et(x) for some x ∈ 𝓑(S)) with (φ_i)_*α_S = α_i, then ε_{k_0} = 1 ⟺ ε_{k_1} = 1.

items.name: Suslin's Hurewicz theorem for K_3 of a field
items.statement: For a field F the Hurewicz map K_3(F) = π_3(BSL(F)^+) → H_3(SL(F), Z) is surjective with kernel {−1}·K_2(F) (Suslin 1990, Cor. 5.2).

items.name: Hutchinson–Tao: H_3(SL_2(F)) surjects onto indecomposable K_3
items.statement: For an infinite field F the composite H_3(SL_2(F), Z) → K_3(F)^ind is surjective (Hutchinson–Tao, Lemma 5.1).

items.name: Lemma 2.10.1: many c_et-liftable classes over a number field
items.statement: For a number field F the image of c_et : H_3(Sp(F), Z) → H^1(F, μ_2) = F^×/2 has at least 2^{r_2(F)} elements, r_2 the number of complex places; already the image of H_3(SL_2(F), Z) does.
items.note: Combines Suslin's Hurewicz theorem, Hutchinson–Tao and Merkurjev–Suslin with Tate's computation that H^1(F, Z_2(2)) has rank r_2 and injectivity of H^1(F, Z_2(2))/2 → H^1(F, μ_2).

items.name: Density of places and controlling extensions
items.statement: For a set 𝒬 of places of a number field, density = liminf_{X→∞} X^{−1} Σ_{q∈𝒬, Nq≤X} log Nq. A finite Galois extension E/L with a nonempty conjugacy-invariant S ⊂ Gal(E/L) is controlling if, among the places v of L unramified in E with Frob_v ∈ S, all but a density-zero set are good (have good residue field).

items.name: Lemma 2.11.1: Reidemeister torsion gives controlling extensions
items.statement: If L is a number field and α ∈ L^×/2 a nontrivial class with α = RT(M, ρ) for a symplectic local system ρ : π_1(M) → Sp_{2r}(L) on a closed oriented 3-manifold, then L(√α)/L with the nontrivial element of its Galois group is controlling.

items.name: Lemma 2.11.2: composita of controlling extensions
items.statement: If (E_i/L, S_i), i = 1, 2, are controlling Galois extensions inside a fixed L̄ (one S_i may be empty), then (E_1E_2/L, S) is controlling, where S is the union of the preimages of S_1 and S_2 under Gal(E_1E_2/L) → Gal(E_1/L) × Gal(E_2/L).

items.name: Lemma 2.11.3: controlling extensions and intermediate fields
items.statement: For E/L Galois, L ⊂ M ⊂ E, S_M ⊂ Gal(E/M) nonempty and conjugacy-invariant, and S_L its conjugacy closure in Gal(E/L): (E/L, S_L) is controlling if and only if (E/M, S_M) is.

items.name: Lemma 2.12.1: liftable classes propagate goodness
items.statement: Let L be a number field and α, β ∈ L^×/2 linearly independent, with β c_et-liftable and L(√α)/L controlling. Then, outside a finite set, every place of L at which β is a nonsquare is good.

items.name: Lemma 2.12.2: adjoining square roots of liftable classes
items.statement: Let α ∈ L^×/2 be nonzero with L(√α)/L controlling, and W ⊂ L^×/2 a finite-dimensional subspace of c_et-liftable classes with W ≠ ⟨α⟩. Then L(√W)/L, with Galois group Hom(W, Z/2) and S its nontrivial elements, is controlling.

items.name: Lemma 2.12.3: one controlling quadratic extension gives density one
items.statement: If K is a number field and K(√α)/K is controlling, then the set of good places of K has density 1.
items.note: Inductive construction of (E_k, S_k) with δ_{k+1} ≤ δ_k − δ_k³/16, using degree-h totally imaginary subextensions of K(ζ_r)/K and Lemmas 2.10.1, 2.11.2, 2.11.3, 2.12.2 (checked).

items.name: §2.13: the good primes of Q have density 1
items.statement: The set of primes p for which F_p is good has density 1.
items.note: Uses the symplectic local system over Q(i) with nonsquare Reidemeister torsion from Appendix C.4.1, Lemma 2.11.1 and Lemma 2.12.3 twice (for Q(i), then for Q with α = −1).

items.name: §2.14: 𝔑 = c_et for finitely generated rings of characteristic zero
items.statement: For every normal integral ring S finitely generated over Z with Z → S injective, 𝔑 = c_et : 𝓑(S) → H^1(S, μ_2).

items.name: §2.15: every finite field of odd characteristic is good
items.statement: For every finite field k of characteristic ≠ 2, 𝔑 = c_et on 𝓑(k); indeed every class in H_3(Sp(k))/2 lifts to H_3(Sp(S^+)) for a normal integral finitely generated S^+ ⊂ W(k) of characteristic zero, by lifting a 2-Sylow subgroup to the Witt vectors.

items.name: 𝔑 = c_et for all normal integral Z[1/2]-algebras
items.statement: 𝔑 = c_et as natural transformations 𝓑 → 𝓗 on finitely generated normal integral Z[1/2]-algebras (in characteristic p by Chebotarev on the F_p-variety Spec S) and on all fields of characteristic ≠ 2 (as direct limits).

items.name: Theorem 2.1: the topological theorem
items.statement: Let M be a closed oriented 3-manifold, K a field of characteristic ≠ 2 and ρ : π_1(M) → Sp_{2r}(K) a symplectic local system. Then (−1)^{χ_{1/2}(M,ρ)/2} RT(M, ρ) = ∫_M ρ^*c_et in K^×/2, where χ_{1/2}(M, ρ) = dim H^0(M, ρ) − dim H^1(M, ρ).

items.name: Vanishing of c_31 on Sp_{2r}(R)
items.statement: The étale Chern class c_31 : H_3(Sp_{2r}(R), Z/2) → H^1_et(R, Z/2) = R^×/2 is zero (Sp_{2r}(R) as a discrete group): β∘c_31 is the Bockstein of c_22, which comes from the metaplectic double cover and lifts to the universal Z-cover, and β : H^1_et(R, Z/2) → H^2_et(R, Z/2) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Used in Lemma 6.3.1 to land in totally positive classes; uses compatibility of étale Chern classes with Bockstein (Soulé IV.3.1).

items.name: L-functions of local systems with finite-field coefficients
items.statement: For a smooth projective curve X over F_q, a finite field ℓ of characteristic ≠ p and ρ : Gal(K̄_X/K_X) → GL(V), V an ℓ-vector space, L(X, ρ, t) = Π_x det(1 − t^{deg x} ρ(F_x) | V^{I_x})^{−1} ∈ ℓ[[t]]^× (F_x geometric Frobenius). It is rational, and for unramified ρ, L(X, ρ, t) = Π_{i=0}^{2} det(1 − tF | H^i(X_{k̄}, ρ))^{(−1)^{i+1}} (Grothendieck–Lefschetz with torsion coefficients, SGA 4½ 'Fonctions L mod ℓ^n' Th. 2.2).

items.name: Functional equation and ε-factors with torsion coefficients
items.statement: L(X, ρ, t) = ε(ρ, t) L(X, ρ^∨, 1/(qt)) with ε(ρ, t) = αt^m (α ∈ ℓ^×, m ∈ Z), and ε(ρ) = Π_x ε_x(ρ, ψ, μ) for an additive character ψ of the adeles and a factorized measure (Deligne, 'Les constantes des équations fonctionnelles', Thm. 7.11, (7.9.1)); ε_x = ε_{0,x}·det(−F_x q^{deg(x)/2} | V^{I_x}) (7.6.3), and ε_{0,x}(ρ ⊗ χ) = ε_{0,x}(χ)^{dim ρ} for unramified ρ of trivial determinant ((5.5.3)).

items.name: The normalized Frobenius is special orthogonal
items.statement: Let ρ : π_1(X) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ) with √q ∈ ℓ fixed and H^0 = H^2 = 0 geometrically. Then H^1(X_{k̄}, ρ) has dimension 2(dim ρ)(g − 1), a symmetric pairing with ⟨Fx, Fy⟩ = q⟨x, y⟩, and F̄ = q^{−1/2}F ∈ SO(H^1): ε(ρ, t) = (−√q t)^{dim H^1} det F̄ and ε(ρ, 1/√q) = 1 for unramified ρ of trivial determinant.
items.note: The printed intermediate formula for ε is off by q^{dim H^1}; see sourceIssues E5.

items.name: The square classes L(X, ρ) and L^*(X, ρ)
items.statement: L(X, ρ) is the image of L(X, ρ, 1/√q) in ℓ^×/2 when nonzero; in general L^*(X, ρ) = spinor norm(F̄) = (h!·det⟨v_i, v_j⟩)^{−1}(d^h/dt^h)L(X, ρ, t)|_{t=1/√q} ∈ ℓ^×/2, where h (even) is the order of vanishing, the dimension of the generalized fixed space of F on H^1(X_{k̄}, ρ), with basis v_1, …, v_h. For GSp-valued ρ^{(g)} with cyclotomic multiplier and ρ = ρ^{(g)}(−1/2), L(X, ρ^{(g)}) is the square class of L(X, ρ^{(g)}, 1) = L(X, ρ, 1/√q).
items.note: The second equality is Zassenhaus's formula (Appendix B.9.1) applied to the even-dimensional H^1 of square discriminant.

items.name: Lemma 3.5.1 and §3.5: square discriminant of H^1
items.statement: For a closed oriented surface Σ and ρ : π_1(Σ) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ), ℓ finite, the quadratic form on H^*(Σ, ρ) (the cup-product form on H^1, and the Poincaré pairing between H^0 and H^2) has square discriminant. Consequently, by lifting to the Witt vectors and to C, H^1(X_{k̄}, ρ) has square discriminant and L(X, ρ) does not depend on the choice of √q.
items.note: Proof: the discriminant is a bordism invariant (a Lagrangian image and dim H^* ≡ 0 mod 4), giving MSO_2(BSp_{2r}(ℓ)) = H_2(Sp_{2r}(ℓ), Z) → ℓ^×/2, which vanishes because H_2 has odd order (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: The trace map and c_et(X, ρ)
items.statement: For A finite of order prime to p, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence and the trace H^2(X_{k̄}, A(1)) ≅ A give trace_X : H^3_et(X, A(1)) ≅ H^1(Gal(k̄/k), A) ≅ A (via the Frobenius generator). For ρ : π_1(X) → Sp(ℓ), c_et(X, ρ) := trace_X(ρ^*c_et) ∈ ℓ^×/2 (A = ℓ^×/2 ≅ Z/2).

items.name: Admissible and GSp-admissible pairs
items.statement: (X, ρ), with X a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over k = F_q and ρ : π_1(X) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ), is admissible if (a1) ρ is geometrically surjective, (a2) q is prime to #Sp_{2r}(ℓ), (a3) q is a square in the prime field of ℓ. It is GSp-admissible (ρ : π_1(X) → GSp_{2r}(ℓ) with cyclotomic multiplier) if (a1)′ the geometric image contains Sp_{2r}(ℓ) and (a2)′ q is prime to #GSp_{2r}(ℓ). Admissible implies GSp-admissible for ρ^{(g)}.

items.name: Theorem 3.1: the main theorem
items.statement: Let (X, ρ) be admissible, #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8) and q ≡ 1 (mod 8). Then L(X, ρ) = c_et(X, ρ) in ℓ^×/2 (with L = L^* when the central value vanishes).
items.note: The proof in v1 does not cover r = 1, #ℓ = 9 (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Equivalence of the Sp and GSp formulations
items.statement: For ρ = ρ^{(g)}(−1/2): L(X, ρ^{(g)}) = L(X, ρ) and c_et(X, ρ^{(g)}) = c_et(X, ρ), since the class on GSp(ℓ) pulls back along π_1(X) → Sp(ℓ) × Ẑ → GSp(ℓ) to c_et ⊗ 1 plus a term in H^2(Sp(ℓ), ℓ^×/2) ⊗ ℓ^×/2 = 0.

items.name: Lemma 3.9.1: even valuation of central values of compatible systems
items.statement: Let {σ_λ : π_1(X) → GSp_{2r}(o_{E,λ})} be a compatible system (traces of Frobenius powers in E, independent of λ ∤ p), with L(X, σ, t) ∈ E(t). If λ ∤ 2p and σ_λ has geometric image Zariski dense in Sp_{2r}, then the valuation at λ of L(X, σ) = L(X, σ, 1), if nonzero, is even.
items.note: The spinor norm of an orthogonal map preserving a unimodular lattice has even valuation (O'Meara 92:5).

items.name: Larsen's big-image theorem for compatible systems
items.statement: For a compatible system {σ_λ} with Zariski-dense image, for a density-one set of λ the image of σ_λ in PSp_{2r}(E_λ) contains a conjugate of the image of Sp_{2r}(o_λ) (Larsen, Thm. 3.17).

items.name: §3.10 (*): Theorem 3.1 determines L-values of compatible systems
items.statement: Let {σ_λ} be a compatible system of GSp_{2r}-valued representations over X/F_q, q ≡ 1 (mod 8), with L(X, σ) ≠ 0, such that (a) the p-cyclotomic extension of E(√2) has degree > 4r² and (b) σ_λ has Zariski-dense image for a density-one set of λ. Then Theorem 3.1 applied to the reductions of σ determines the square class of L(X, σ) in E(√q)^×/2 up to multiplication by 2.
items.note: Not used elsewhere in the paper.

items.name: The defect δ(X, ρ) and Frobenius of k
items.statement: δ(X, ρ) := L^*(X, ρ)/c_et(X, ρ) ∈ ℓ^×/2 (similarly for GSp-admissible ρ^{(g)}). For M/Q finite Galois unramified at p, Frob_k ∈ Gal(M/Q) is the conjugacy class of Frob(ϖ/p)^n for q = p^n.

items.name: Step A: the defect is a Dirichlet character
items.statement: For fixed r and ℓ there is a quadratic character χ_{r,ℓ} : Gal(Q̄/Q) → {±1}, unramified outside the primes dividing #Sp_{2r}(ℓ), such that δ(X, ρ) = χ_{r,ℓ}(Frob_k) (under {±1} ≅ ℓ^×/2) for every GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k.
items.note: The proof uses Lemma 5.1.1, which fails for r = 1, #ℓ = 9 (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Step B: χ_{r,ℓ} is unramified outside 2ℓ
items.statement: For #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8), the character χ_{r,ℓ} of Step A is unramified outside 2ℓ: for each odd prime m ≠ ℓ there is a Galois extension M* of Q unramified at m such that for every sufficiently large prime p split in M* there is a GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over F_{p^j}, j odd, with δ(X, ρ) = 1.

items.name: Steps A and B imply Theorem 3.1
items.statement: If χ_{r,ℓ} is unramified outside 2ℓ then χ_{r,ℓ}(Frob_p) = (Z/p) with Z ∈ ⟨−1, 2, ℓ_0⟩; writing Z = Z_0 or Z_0ℓ_0′ (ℓ_0′ = (−1)^{(ℓ_0−1)/2}ℓ_0) and using (ℓ_0′/p)^n = (q/ℓ_0) = 1 for admissible (X, ρ), δ(X, ρ) = (Z_0/p)^n, a character mod 8 of q = p^n, which is 1 when q ≡ 1 (mod 8).

items.name: Hurwitz stacks 𝔐^G_g and 𝔐^{G*}_g
items.statement: For G = Sp_{2r}(ℓ), N = #G: the Deligne–Mumford stack 𝔐^G_g over Z[1/N] of smooth projective genus-g curves Σ/S with a finite étale G-torsor f : Σ̃ → Σ whose geometric fibres Σ̃_s are irreducible; and its twisted form 𝔐^{G*}_g for G̃ = GSp_{2r}(ℓ) with an identification of the associated ℓ^×-cover with the cyclotomic one (fibres with #ℓ − 1 components). Over C a component is 𝒯/Γ̃_0 for Teichmüller space 𝒯 and the central extension Γ̃_0 of the stabilizer Γ_0 of a surjection π_1(Σ) → G by Z(G); 𝔐^G_g is a gerbe over Deligne–Mumford's stack of Teichmüller level structures. Admissible pairs give k-points of 𝔐^G_g, GSp-admissible pairs k-points of 𝔐^{G*}_g.

items.name: Livingston–Dunfield–Thurston: mapping class group orbits on surjections
items.statement: For a finite group G with H_2(G, Z) = 0 and g sufficiently large, the mapping class group of a closed genus-g surface Σ acts transitively on the set of conjugacy classes of surjections π_1(Σ) → G (Dunfield–Thurston, Thm. 6.25, after Livingston). In general the orbits are classified by the image of [Σ] in H_2(G, Z).
items.note: The paper notes that Dunfield–Thurston's Theorem 6.25 is slightly misstated (the action is by the mapping class group modulo the group).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.1: irreducibility in large genus
items.statement: If H_2(Sp_{2r}(ℓ), Z) = 0, i.e. unless r = 1 and #ℓ = 9, there is g_0(r, ℓ) such that for g ≥ g_0 the Q̄-fibre of 𝔐^G_g is irreducible (and so is that of 𝔐^{G*}_g).
items.note: Stated as corrected; the paper asserts it for all (r, ℓ) (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: The universal classes 𝔜 and 𝔜′
items.statement: On the universal curve π : 𝔘* → 𝔐^{G*} with its G̃-cover 𝔘* → BG̃: 𝔜 ∈ H^1_et(𝔐^{G*}, Z/2) is π_*(pullback of c_et) (trace shifting degree by 2), and 𝔜′ ∈ H^1(𝔐^{G*}, ℓ^×/2) classifies the spinor-norm torsor of the orthogonal local system 𝒪 = R^1π_*𝒮 (𝒮 the symplectic ℓ-local system, with pairing to ℓ(1)). For a GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k, 𝔜 and 𝔜′ specialize to c_et(X, ρ) and L(X, ρ) in H^1(k, Z/2) = k^×/2.
items.note: Uses étale cohomology of Artin stacks (Laszlo–Olsson).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.1: 𝔜 = 𝔜′ on the geometric generic fibre
items.statement: 𝔜 and 𝔜′ coincide on 𝔐^{G*}_{Q̄}.
items.note: For a loop γ, 𝔜(γ) = trace_M(ρ^*c_et) on the mapping torus M and 𝔜′(γ) = spinor norm of the monodromy on H^1(fibre, ρ), equal by (1.5); here the coefficients are finite, where the paper proves (1.5) only in characteristic 0 (sourceIssues E25). The stack is handled through a smooth cover (Y × E)/Δ with E an approximation of BΔ (Totaro).

items.name: Lemma 5.3.1: 𝔜 − 𝔜′ comes from Z[1/N]
items.statement: For g ≥ g_0(r, ℓ), 𝔜 − 𝔜′ is the pullback to 𝔐^{G*} of a class in H^1(Z[1/N], Z/2), i.e. of a quadratic character unramified outside N.
items.note: Uses irreducibility (Lemma 5.1.1), purity (injectivity of H^1(𝔐^{G*}) → H^1(𝔐^{G*}_Q)) and W-points of 𝔐^{G*} for each w ∤ N (Sp_{2r}(ℓ) is 2-generated).

items.name: §5.4 Claim: odd-degree cyclic covers preserve δ
items.statement: Let (X, ρ) be GSp-admissible, m odd and prime to ℓ with ℓ of odd order t modulo m, and f : X̃ → X a Z/m-Galois cover by a geometrically irreducible smooth proper curve. Then (X̃, f^*ρ) is GSp-admissible and δ(X, ρ) = δ(X̃, f^*ρ).
items.note: c_et is preserved since f^* : H^3(X, Z/2) → H^3(X̃, Z/2) is an isomorphism; for L^* the Artin decomposition over the characters of Z/m, the functional equation and §5.4.1 show the extra factors are squares.

items.name: §5.4.1: ε-factors of twists of symplectic systems
items.statement: For ρ symplectic and unramified with det ρ = 1 and χ a character, ε(ρ ⊗ χ) = ε(χ)^{dim ρ} (an equality, not only of square classes); in particular ε(ρ ⊗ χ) is a square.

items.name: §5.5 Claim: raising the genus
items.statement: For each GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k there is g_0′(X, ρ) such that for every g ≥ g_0′ there is a GSp-admissible (X′, ρ′) of genus g over k with δ(X′, ρ′) = δ(X, ρ).
items.note: X′ is a ramified Z/M-cover, M a product of primes m ≡ 3 (mod 4) with q and ℓ of odd order mod m and gcd of the (m−1)/2 equal to 1, built by class field theory and Riemann–Hurwitz.

items.name: §6.1 Claim: totally real fields with prescribed unit reduction
items.statement: For a finite field ℓ with #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8) and an odd prime m ≠ char ℓ, there is a totally real field F with (i) [F:Q] ≥ 3, (ii) D_F prime to m, (iii) a prime λ_0 with o_F/λ_0 ≅ ℓ such that U_F^+ (totally positive classes in H^1(o_F[1/2], Z/2) ⊂ F^×/2) maps trivially to ℓ^×/2, and (iv) a Galois extension M ⊃ F of Q unramified at m such that for every p unramified, prime to 2ℓ and completely split in M, U_F^{(p+)} also maps trivially to ℓ^×/2.
items.note: F = Q[x]/f for f = x^n + Σa_i x^{n−i} ± ℓ with real roots, roots ≡ 1 (mod 8) in Q_2, a prescribed ℓ_0-adic factorization, discriminant prime to m and irreducible; λ_0 = (α) with α a square at the places above 2.

items.name: Compatible systems on the Hilbert–Siegel variety
items.statement: For each place λ of F with residue characteristic prime to Δ, 𝒮[1/λ] carries the étale local system ρ_λ of o_{F,λ}-modules from the Tate module of the universal abelian scheme, pure of weight −1, coming over C from a local system of o_F-modules; at an F_q-point (q prime to Δ) the trace of Frobenius on ρ_λ lies in F and is independent of λ (Shimura, 11.10). The geometric image of ρ_λ is Sp_{2r}(o_{F,λ}) for λ ∤ e, and Zariski dense for λ | e.

items.name: Vanishing of H^1 of the Hilbert–Siegel variety
items.statement: H^1(S_C, ρ_λ) = 0; equivalently H^1(Γ, F^{2r} ⊗_ι C) = 0 for an arithmetic Γ ≤ Sp_{2r}(F) and each embedding ι : F → C.
items.note: The paper sketches this from superrigidity or the congruence subgroup property ([F:Q] ≥ 3 gives real rank ≥ 3).

items.name: Lemma 6.3.1: α_C = 0
items.statement: Let α ∈ H^3_et(𝒮, ℓ^×/2) be the pullback of c_et along the reduction of ρ_{λ_0} (a GSp_{2r}(ℓ)-local system). Its restriction to S_C is trivial.
items.note: Over C the local system lifts to Sp_{2r}(o_F); c_et then factors through U_F, landing in U_F^+ by the vanishing of c_31 on Sp_{2r}(R), and U_F^+ → ℓ^×/2 is trivial by §6.1 (iii).

items.name: Lemma 6.3.2: killing α on special fibres
items.statement: There is a finite Galois extension M/Q, unramified outside 2Δ (so at m), such that Frob_k trivial in Gal(M/Q) implies α_k = 0.
items.note: Rπ_*(Z/2) on Z[1/Δ] has lcc cohomology sheaves (via the normal crossings compactification, SGA 4½ 'Théorèmes de finitude', appendix); M is the maximal exponent-2 abelian extension, unramified outside 2Δ, of the splitting field of H^2(S_Q̄, Z/2).

items.name: Slicing down to a surface
items.statement: For a geometrically irreducible component S° ⊂ P^m_{M_0} (M_0 = Q(ζ_e)) of dimension ≥ 3 whose boundary in its closure has codimension ≥ 3, a general M_0-rational hyperplane section is smooth, geometrically irreducible, has boundary codimension ≥ 3, and induces an isomorphism on π_1 of the complex points (Goresky–MacPherson, Stratified Morse Theory II.1.1), hence on H^1(−, ρ_λ). Iterating, one reaches a smooth projective surface with the same properties (a)–(d) of §6.4, which spread out over o_{M_0}[1/S] and specialize to F_p for large p split in M_0 (geometric monodromy preserved by SGA 1 X; H^1 = 0 by proper smooth base change).

items.name: Guralnick–Tiep: the eighth-moment criterion for SO
items.statement: For a reductive algebraic subgroup Γ ⊂ O(W), W orthogonal over a field of characteristic zero (of large enough dimension), dim(W^{⊗8})^Γ = dim(W^{⊗8})^{SO(W)} = C_4 = 8!/(4!·2^4) implies Γ ⊃ SO(W) (Guralnick–Tiep, Thm. 1.4).

items.name: Lemma 6.4.2: points impose independent conditions on hypersurfaces
items.statement: For pairwise distinct x_1, …, x_r in S°(F_q) and D ≥ r − 1, vanishing at all x_i is a codimension-r condition on Γ(S°_{F_q}, 𝒪(D)) (Poonen, Lemma 2.1), so the fraction of degree-D slices through them is (q^{E−r} − 1)/(q^E − 1) = q^{−r}(1 + O(q^{r−E})), E = dim Γ(S°, 𝒪(D)).
items.note: Stated as corrected: the paper's choice of D does not guarantee D ≥ r − 1 (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: Lemma 6.4.1: slices with nonvanishing central value
items.statement: There are D_0 and p_0(D) such that for D ≥ D_0 and p ≥ p_0(D) split in M_0, the orthogonal local system 𝖶 (fibre H^1(X_h, ρ_λ)(−1)) on the space ℋ_D of smooth degree-D slices of the surface S°_{F_p} has geometric monodromy Zariski dense in SO; and there are an odd j and h ∈ ℋ_D(F_{p^j}) with slice X = X_h a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve such that (i) L(X, ρ_λ, 1) ≠ 0, (ii) the geometric monodromy of (X, ρ_λ) equals that of (S°, ρ_λ), (iii) j is odd.
items.note: Method of moments: the eighth moment of the Frobenius traces on H^1(X_h, ρ_λ) over ℋ_D is bounded by C_4 q^4(1 + o(1)) using Lemma 6.4.2, Deligne's bound (6.15) and a Möbius inversion over set partitions; then Guralnick–Tiep and Chebotarev. (ii) is Grothendieck's Lefschetz theorem (SGA 2 XII Cor. 3.5).

items.name: Lemma 6.5.1: c_et of the slices
items.statement: There is a Galois extension M_1/Q, unramified at m, such that for the slices (X, ρ) of Lemma 6.4.1 (ρ the reduction of ρ_{λ_0}), c_et(X, ρ) is trivial whenever p is split in M_1.
items.note: The printed statement says 'unramified outside m' (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: Lemma 6.5.2: L-value of the slices
items.statement: There is a Galois extension M_2/Q, unramified at m, such that L(X, ρ) is trivial whenever p is split in M_2 and sufficiently large: L(X, ρ_·, 1) ∈ F^× is totally positive (Riemann hypothesis) with even valuation at every λ ∤ 2p (Lemma 3.9.1), so its class lies in U_F^{(p+)}, which maps trivially to ℓ^×/2 by §6.1 (iv).

items.name: Sign conventions for complexes, and ε-symmetric (Poincaré) complexes
items.statement: Over a commutative ring R with 1/2, for bounded complexes of projective modules with increasing differential: the Koszul tensor product and swap (x_n ⊗ y_m ↦ (−1)^{nm} y_m ⊗ x_n); R[k] in degree −k; C[1] := R[1] ⊗ C with negated differential; the dual C^∨ with C^∨_{−q} = C_q^* and differential (−1)^{q+1}d^*_{−1−q} (A.2); (C[1])^∨ ≅ C^∨[−1] via (−1)^q in degree q (A.3); cones D ⊕ C[1] (A.4) and cone(f)^∨ ≅ cone(f^∨)[−1] (A.5). An ε-symmetric complex of dimension n is a finite locally free complex with an ε-symmetric chain map T : C ⊗ C → R[−n] (T_{p,q} = ε(−1)^{pq}T_{q,p}, (A.6)); it is Poincaré if the adjoint f : C → C^∨[−n] is a quasi-isomorphism and strict if f is an isomorphism. Shifting by 1 turns an ε-symmetric complex of dimension n into a (−ε)-symmetric one of dimension n − 2 (Remark A.1).
items.note: Follows Ranicki's algebraic surgery; checked by hand except the cone-duality signs, which the paper only partly writes out.

items.name: Poincaré complexes of manifolds and of the circle
items.statement: For an n-manifold M with a self-dual ε-symmetric local system ρ and a cell structure, Poincaré duality with the dual cell structure, transferred by a homotopy equivalence and symmetrized as ½(⟨x, y⟩ ± ⟨y, x⟩), makes C^*(M, ρ) an ε-symmetric Poincaré complex of dimension n. For M = S^1 and A ∈ SO(V), C = [V →(1−A) V] with the pairings ½⟨(1+A)−, −⟩ on C_0 ⊗ C_1 and ½⟨(1+A^{−1})−, −⟩ on C_1 ⊗ C_0.

items.name: The algebraic boundary of a symmetric complex
items.statement: For an ε-symmetric complex C of dimension n with adjoint f : C → C^∨[−n] (not necessarily Poincaré), the cone D of f is a strict ε-symmetric Poincaré complex of dimension n − 1, fitting into the diagram (A.9) of short exact sequences C^∨[−n] → D → C[1] and C^∨[−n] → D^∨[1−n] → C^{∨∨}[1]; for C = C^*_c(M) the cone is C^*(∂M).
items.note: The paper asserts the pairing on D 'by explicit computation' without writing it; the signs of (A.9) were not checked.

items.name: Semicharacteristic of strict Poincaré complexes and its constancy
items.statement: For a 1-dimensional symmetric Poincaré complex over a field, χ_{1/2}(C) := Σ_{j≤0}(−1)^j dim H^j(C) (A.10) (and by shifting for (2n+1)-dimensional (−1)^n-symmetric complexes); if C is strict then χ_{1/2}(C) ≡ Σ_{j≤0} dim C_j (mod 2) (A.11). Over a ring R with 1/2, Zariski locally every ε-symmetric Poincaré complex is quasi-isomorphic, compatibly with the pairing, to a strict one (A.6.2), and the semicharacteristic of the fibres C ⊗ k(𝔭) mod 2 is locally constant on Spec R (after Sorger, Thm. 0.1).
items.note: The proof of (A.11) as printed has a false step (sourceIssues E12); the claim itself holds.

items.name: Splitting strict 1-symmetric complexes over a field
items.statement: Over a field, a strict 1-symmetric complex C (symmetric isomorphism C ≅ C^∨[−1]) splits compatibly with the duality as Q ⊕ Q^∨[−1] ⊕ R, with Q = τ_{≤0}C (quasi-isomorphically) and R a strict 1-symmetric acyclic complex E_0 →(d) B_1 in degrees 0 and 1.
items.note: The displayed table of degrees is shifted by one (sourceIssues E13).

items.name: Graded lines, inverses and square classes
items.statement: The symmetric monoidal category of graded k-lines (L, n), n ∈ Z/2, with commutativity sign (−1)^{nn′}; unordered tensor products; (L, n)^{−1} = (L^∨, −n) with (L ⊗ M)^{−1} ≅ M^{−1} ⊗ L^{−1} (B.1) and (λ^{−1})^{−1} = (−1)^n λ (B.2). A square class in L is a nonzero element up to k^{×2}; L ⊗ L carries a distinguished square class; square classes of M^{−1} and M correspond (B.3); the swap [L]^{⊗2} → L_1^{⊗2} ⊗ L_2^{⊗2} introduces (−1)^{d_1d_2} (B.4).
items.note: Following Knudsen–Mumford's conventions.

items.name: The determinant functor and its shift and duality isomorphisms
items.statement: A Knudsen–Mumford determinant functor det = [−] from bounded complexes and quasi-isomorphisms to Z/2-graded lines, with compatibility with short exact sequences and normalization on vector spaces, fixed once and for all; the acyclic volume form; [A ⊕ B] ≅ [A][B] up to (−1)^{χ(A)χ(B)} (B.5); θ : [C[1]] ≅ [C]^{−1} (from C → cone(1_C) → C[1], (B.6)) and θ_n; 𝔡 : [C^∨] ≅ [C]^{−1}; on vector spaces the 'exotic' duality 𝒜 : v_1 ∧ … ∧ v_n ↦ (v_n^* ∧ … ∧ v_1^*)^{−1} (B.7), the standard one twisted by (−1)^{n(n−1)/2}, which is compatible with short exact sequences; and compatibility of 𝔡 with θ (B.8).
items.note: The paper's duality normalization differs from the standard one (B.24) by (−1)^{n(n−1)/2}.

items.name: Determinants of strongly even complexes
items.statement: On strongly even complexes (even-dimensional in every degree) and isomorphisms, there is a natural isomorphism [C] ≅ ⊗_j [C_j]^{(−1)^j} (B.13), built from brutal truncations, under which the short-exact-sequence isomorphisms, θ and 𝔡 become the term-by-term ones (𝔡 becoming 𝒜 degree by degree).
items.note: The truncation sequence (B.14) is misprinted (sourceIssues E14).

items.name: The determinant of a complex and of its cohomology
items.statement: A natural isomorphism [C] ≅ [H^*C] on complexes over a field and quasi-isomorphisms, determined by the cases of zero differential and of acyclic complexes via B → Z → H and Z → C → B[1]; it is compatible with shifts and duality (B.15) and with split short exact sequences (B.16). For an injection α : A → B with cone C, the isomorphism [A][C] ≅ [B] from C ≃ B/A agrees with the one from B → C → A[1] and θ (B.17).

items.name: Lagrangians and their volume classes
items.statement: For W with an ε-symmetric perfect pairing and a Lagrangian L, L → W → L^* and 𝒜 give a class in [W]; it is independent of L if W is symplectic, and depends only on the component of the Lagrangian Grassmannian if W is orthogonal. For odd n, a strict ε-symmetric complex C of dimension n and a Lagrangian ι : L → C (L → C → L^∨[−n] short exact, (B.18)), the isomorphism [C] ≅ [L][L^∨[−n]] ≅ [L]^{⊗2} (B.19) defines a square class ν_L ∈ [C]. For strongly even L it is the product of the degree-wise classes of L_j ⊕ L_{n−j} ⊂ C_j ⊕ C_{n−j}, and it is multiplicative for direct sums (with an extra (−1)^{d_1d_2} if the L_i are not strongly even).

items.name: (B.20): comparing the volume classes of an algebraic boundary
items.statement: Let C be a strongly even skew-symmetric complex of dimension n = 2k, k even, and D the cone of f : C → C^∨[−n], a strict skew-symmetric Poincaré complex of dimension 2k − 1. The volume classes on D from (a) the Lagrangian C^∨[−n] ⊂ D, (b) the brutal truncation σ_{≥k}D and (c) [D] ≅ [H^*D] with the Lagrangian σ_{≥k}H^*D satisfy (a) = (b) = (−1)^r (c), r = (χ(C) + χ_{1/2}(D))/2.
items.note: Stated as corrected: the paper names the Lagrangian in (a) as C (sourceIssues E15). The proof splits D by Appendix A.7; the dimension count (B.22)–(B.23) was checked mod 4.

items.name: The Reidemeister class e_X and duality
items.statement: For a (2k−1)-manifold X (possibly with boundary) and a 2d-dimensional local system with pairing of parity (−1)^{k+1} (symplectic with its Pfaffian volume form, or orthogonal with a self-dual volume form for the standard duality (B.24)), a triangulation gives distinguished classes e_X ∈ [C^*(X, ρ)] and e_{X,∂X}, independent of the triangulation. Under Poincaré duality PD : [C_X] → [C_{X,∂X}^∨[−n]] → [C_{X,∂X}]^{(−1)^{n+1}} (B.26), e_X ↦ (−1)^{d·χ(X)} e_{X,∂X}^{(−1)^{n+1}} (B.27). RT(X, ρ) is e_X divided by the class (c) of Appendix B.6 on [H^*(X, ρ)].
items.note: The sign in (B.27) was not independently checked. The definition's cross-reference is misprinted (sourceIssues E16).

items.name: Zassenhaus's formula for the spinor norm
items.statement: For A ∈ SO(V), V even-dimensional of square discriminant over K (char ≠ 2), with V = V^+ ⊕ V^− ⊕ W the generalized (+1)-, (−1)- and remaining eigenspaces: the generalized ±1-eigenspaces and the fixed spaces of ±A are even-dimensional, and spinor norm(A) = det(1 − A)|_W · disc(V^+) in K^×/2 (B.31). In characteristic 0, V^+ decomposes A-equivariantly into orthogonal sums E_1 ⊕ E_2 of odd Jordan blocks and E ⊕ E^* with E an even Jordan block (Jacobson–Morozov).
items.note: Zassenhaus, Arch. Math. 13 (1962). The identity was checked numerically on 60 random examples.

items.name: Lemma C.2.1: Reidemeister torsion of mapping tori
items.statement: Let S be a closed oriented surface, t a mapping class, M the mapping torus, and ρ : π_1(S) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ) with ρ(t(g)) = Mρ(g)M^{−1} (C.1), so that ρ extends to M. If H^0(S, ρ) = 0 and char ℓ = 0, the induced T on H^1(S, ρ) has determinant 1 and (−1)^{h/2} RT(M, ρ) = spinor norm(T), h the (even) dimension of the fixed space of T (= dim H^1(M, ρ)). Equivalently (C.2), (−1)^{h/2} RT(M, ρ) = det′(1 − T)·δ, det′ on the complement of the generalized 1-eigenspace and δ the discriminant of the form on the generalized 1-eigenspace.
items.note: δ stated as corrected (the paper takes the fixed space; sourceIssues E20). The proof reduces to the circle via the triangle C^*(M) → V[−1] →(1−T) V[−1].

items.name: (1.5): the spinor norm of a mapping class
items.statement: For a closed oriented surface Σ, a symplectic local system ρ of ℓ-vector spaces with H^0(Σ, ρ) = 0, and a mapping class f with an isomorphism f^*ρ ≅ ρ extending ρ to ρ_f on the mapping torus M_f: spinor norm(f^* : H^1(Σ, ρ) → H^1(Σ, ρ)) = trace_{M_f}(ρ_f^*c_et) in ℓ^×/2.
items.locator: §1.1, (1.5), p. 3; deduced from Theorem 2.1 and Lemma C.2.1
items.note: Proved in the paper only when char ℓ = 0 (through Lemma C.2.1); Lemma 5.2.1 uses it for finite ℓ (sourceIssues E25).

items.name: Cocycle model for H^1 of a genus-2 surface and det(1 − T)
items.statement: For π_1(S) = ⟨a_1, b_1, a_2, b_2 | [a_1, b_1][a_2, b_2]⟩, 1-cocycles are determined by φ(a_1), φ(b_1), φ(a_2), φ(b_2) subject to (C.5); if ρ(b_1) has no eigenvalue 1, H^1(S, ρ) ≅ coker(V → V^{⊕3}, v ↦ (b_1v − v, a_2v − v, b_2v − v)) (C.6); T acts by φ ↦ M^{−1}∘φ∘t, and when T has no eigenvalue 1, det(1 − T) = det(1 − T̃ | V^{⊕3})/det(1 − M^{−1} | V) (C.9). The Dehn twists T_1, …, T_5 of C.1 act on π_1 as printed.
items.note: The composition convention for words in the T_i is not stated; the printed matrices use the leftmost factor first (sourceIssues E21).

items.name: A symplectic local system over Q(i) with nonsquare Reidemeister torsion
items.statement: For the genus-2 mapping torus of t = T_4²T_2T_3T_1 and ρ with values in the binary tetrahedral group Ã_4 ⊂ SL_2(Q(i)), a_1 ↦ diag(−i, i), b_1, a_2 ↦ −I, b_2 ↦ ½[[−1−i, −1−i], [1−i, −1+i]], M = [[0, −1], [1, 0]]: T has characteristic polynomial x⁴ + 1, h = 0, det(1 − T̃) = 4, det(1 − M^{−1}) = 2, and RT(M, ρ) = 2 ~ i, a nonsquare in Q(i)^×/2. A second example (t = T_5²T_4T_5², C.4.2) has square torsion 4.
items.note: Reproduced exactly (the 6×6 matrices and determinants), reading the word for t with its leftmost twist applied first. This example is the single input 'by hand' for §2.13.

items.name: c_et on the quaternion group
items.statement: The pullback of the étale Chern class from H^3(SL_2(Q(i)), Q(i)^×/2) to Q_8 (Pauli matrices) is the unique nonzero class of H^3(Q_8, Z/2), valued in the subgroup generated by i: for q ≡ 5 (mod 8), Q_8 is a 2-Sylow subgroup of SL_2(F_q) and H_3(Q_8) → H_3(SL_2(F_q)) is onto, while i is a nonsquare in F_q.

items.name: Both sides of Theorem 3.1 for quaternionic covers of curves
items.statement: A Q_8-cover of a curve X/F_q is a quadratic étale X̃/X with involution σ and α : Pic(X̃) → Z/4 with σ^*α = −α and α|_{Pic X} the character of X̃/X (D.1). Then ∫_X of the generator of H^3(Q_8) equals y(ℒ_x), y ∈ H^1(X, Z/2) evaluated by class field theory on the 2-torsion bundle of x (Lemma D.4.1: ∫x² ∪ y = ∫β′(x) ∪ y, (D.2)); and L(X, ρ, 1/√q) = L(X̃, α, 1/√q) = Σ_k q^{−k/2}L_k with L_k = Σ_{deg D=k} α(D), symmetric under k ↔ 2g − 2 − k with sign α(𝒦). For genus-2 X : y² = xQ(x) with X̃ : w² = Q(t²) this gives qL(½, ρ) = 2q + Σ_{deg D=2} α(D) (D.6), and the invariant (D.5) vanishes iff (0) − (∞) ∈ π_*(ker α²).
items.note: Several slips in D.2–D.6 are recorded as sourceIssues E22–E24.

items.name: Numerical examples beyond the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1
items.statement: Each of the hyperelliptic curves 2x⁸ + 2x⁶z² − 4x⁴z⁴ − 3x²z⁶ − 3z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_5, x⁸ + 4x⁶z² + 2x⁴z⁴ + 3x²z⁶ + 5z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_11, 5x⁸ + 2x⁶z² − 6x⁴z⁴ − 7x²z⁶ + 7z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_13 and 5x⁸ + 15x⁶z² + 15x⁴z⁴ + 2x²z⁶ + 12z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_17 carries a quaternionic local system with nonsquare qL(½) and nonvanishing invariant (D.5); in all computed examples 'qL(½) is a square' coincided with vanishing of (D.5).
items.note: Recomputed independently (class groups and all 8 admissible α per curve): every nonzero qL(½) is ~ i and the pairing is nonzero; on the F_5 curve 4 of the 8 α have L(½) = 0, a case the paper does not discuss.
